- `FINDING_ID: F001; SEVERITY: 0.98; FLAW_CLASS: 1; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.93; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1119](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1119), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1202](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1202), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2783](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2783). DESCRIPTION: `current_round` stays `0` in `SYNTH`, so `process_round()` records both BLIND and SYNTH as round 0. I reproduced two successive calls yielding stored round indexes `[0, 0]`, and the second call overwrote `ConvergenceDetector._round_findings[0]`. That corrupts convergence, diminishing-returns, and audit history. PROPOSED_FIX: give every processed phase a unique index, or separate phase state from round index and never key round data by the mutable FSM state alone. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F002; SEVERITY: 0.96; FLAW_CLASS: 1; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.95; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L462](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L462), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L848](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L848), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2691](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2691), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2937](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2937). DESCRIPTION: the advertised adaptive routing loop is effectively disconnected. I changed live fingerprints from very strong to very weak and `get_allocation()` returned the same allocation before and after, because `LoadBalancer` never reads fingerprints or task/flaw-class capability fit, and role reassignment still scores against the original `_models`. PROPOSED_FIX: make allocation and reassignment consume live capability data directly, including task-to-capability matching, instead of only load fraction. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F003; SEVERITY: 0.93; FLAW_CLASS: 5; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L721](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L721), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L743](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L743). DESCRIPTION: critical-task redundancy is computed against total models `K`, but PM is excluded from admissible workers when `K > 1`. In a 3-model pool with 1 PM and 2 workers, a critical task gets target `3` while only `2` models are actually assignable. PROPOSED_FIX: compute redundancy against admissible active workers, not raw model count. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F004; SEVERITY: 0.91; FLAW_CLASS: 5; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L797](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L797), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L848](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L848). DESCRIPTION: redundancy targets are treated as best-effort only and are never validated. I reproduced a critical task with target `3` that was assigned to only `['a', 'b']`, yet `_check_feasibility()` still returned `(True, [])`. That silently weakens protection exactly where the task is marked most critical. PROPOSED_FIX: add an explicit redundancy constraint/check and report unmet redundancy as infeasible or at least as a first-class degraded-allocation state. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F005; SEVERITY: 0.89; FLAW_CLASS: 5; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1624](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1624), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1696](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1696). DESCRIPTION: the “no findings” case is documented as “not converged unless null_expected”, but the implementation returns full convergence. I reproduced `kappa_set=1.0`, `kappa_rate=1.0`, `kappa_adopt=1.0`, `converged=True` for three empty rounds. That lets total silence be reported as success. PROPOSED_FIX: add an explicit empty-evidence guard in `converged()` or a `null_expected` flag that must be true before empty rounds can converge. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F006; SEVERITY: 0.87; FLAW_CLASS: 1; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1757](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1757), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2834](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2834). DESCRIPTION: diminishing-returns yield is inflated by duplicate findings across rounds. I reproduced a case where the same finding repeated in round 1 gave `kappa_set=1.0` but cumulative yield still rose from `1.0` to `2.0`, producing `mu1=1.0`. That rewards repetition and delays stopping. PROPOSED_FIX: compute yield from novel equivalence classes or novelty-weighted classes, not flattened class members from all rounds. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

DESCRIPTION: most recovery actions are never actually carried out. `get_recovery()` can return `RETRY`, `RETRY_EXTENDED`, `RETRY_CLARIFIED`, `DEGRADE`, `DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, and `REALLOCATE`, but `process_round()` only treats `ABORT` specially; the rest are effectively inert except `EXCLUDE`, which is handled inside `FailureHandler`. PROPOSED_FIX: return or execute a concrete recovery plan from `process_round()`, wire role downgrades/retries/reallocations into manager state, and emit the corresponding recovery events. - `FINDING_ID: F008; SEVERITY: 0.80; FLAW_CLASS: 4; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1823](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1823), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1837](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1837). - `FINDING_ID: F010; SEVERITY: 0.75; FLAW_CLASS: 5; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2149](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2149), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2262](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2262). DESCRIPTION: failure escalation is off by one. With `n_fail=2`, I reproduced PM timeout recovery as `RETRY`, `RETRY`, then `ABORT`; escalation happens on the third occurrence because `same_type_count` is checked before recording the current failure. PROPOSED_FIX: evaluate repetition as `same_type_count + 1 >= n_fail`, or record first and then test the threshold. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F011; SEVERITY: 0.73; FLAW_CLASS: 6; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L721](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L721), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2233](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2233), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2711](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2711). DESCRIPTION: the PM-only degraded mode can be falsely marked inadmissible if `role_map` still contains excluded models. I reproduced a single live PM with stale extra roles producing admissibility mask `[[0]]` and an `F3` violation even though the PM was the only available executor. PROPOSED_FIX: derive admissibility from `self.models` or active-model membership, not from the full historical `role_map`. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F012; SEVERITY: 0.69; FLAW_CLASS: 5; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2358](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2358), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2395](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2395). - `FINDING_ID: F013; SEVERITY: 0.63; FLAW_CLASS: 3; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1345](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1345), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L1481](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1481). DESCRIPTION: equivalence classes can merge findings from different `flaw_class` values, but the resulting class stores only `members[0].flaw_class`. I reproduced one merged class reported as flaw class `1` while its members were `[1, 2]`. That distorts class-level weighting and any downstream reporting by flaw class. PROPOSED_FIX: either forbid cross-class merges or store a set/canonicalised label instead of a single borrowed class id. VERIFIED: TRUE.`

- `FINDING_ID: F014; SEVERITY: 0.56; FLAW_CLASS: 4; ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74; LOCATION: [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2758](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2758), [bench/dynamic_management.py#L2888](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2888). DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` accepts `tasks` but never uses them, and `RoundResult.allocation` is always stored as `None`. PROPOSED_FIX: pass the actual `Allocation` into `process_round()` and persist it in `RoundResult`; use it to detect missing responses and drive reallocation logic. VERIFIED: TRUE.`
